currentContext.expansion: International Travel House is an asset-light travel services business and the routed sections disclose no plant, capacity or rupee capital-expenditure programme. The only physical asset build-out described is in Car Rental Services, where the Company states it continued the phased induction of electric and hybrid vehicles into its fleet in line with its sustainability objectives, with no quantum or timeline given. Beyond the fleet, the stated expansion intent is capability rather than capacity: advancing digital transformation initiatives in car rental, and going forward strengthening the technology platform, expanding service capabilities and deepening client engagement across the mobility ecosystem. In travel management the Company describes technology-led initiatives that strengthen digital servicing capabilities, expense management integration and automated carbon-tracking, with the Self-Booking Tool and embedded corporate card programmes being rolled out. The Company has no subsidiary, associate or joint venture, and no acquisition, new site or geographic addition is disclosed in this material.

risks.risk: Geopolitical disruption to travel demand and cross-border mobility
risks.note: Management states the operating landscape shifted materially in the latter part of the year as tariff measures, escalating trade tensions, Rupee volatility and geopolitical developments including the conflict in West Asia heightened uncertainty; for the travel industry these influenced consumer sentiments, fuel prices, route economics and cross-border mobility.

risks.risk: Fuel price and route economics exposure
risks.note: The same paragraph identifies fuel prices and route economics as the channel through which external shocks reach the travel industry, a structural cost/pricing exposure for a company whose revenue is built on air ticketing and chauffeur-driven mobility.
Volatility in the Indian Rupee is named among the factors that materially shifted the operating landscape - relevant given the outbound leisure and outbound MICE exposure.

risks.risk: Moderating growth in Indian domestic air traffic
risks.note: Domestic air traffic growth slowed to 3.48% year-on-year in 2025 from 6.12% in 2024 (DGCA); management notes the pace of expansion moderated amid external uncertainties and operational constraints, and the Company's travel management volumes track this base.

risks.risk: Outbound MICE and international delegate participation disruption
risks.note: Management states geopolitical tensions and travel-related disruptions have affected outbound event timelines and international delegate participation, leaving the outbound half of the MICE business exposed even while domestic MICE stays resilient.

risks.risk: Air connectivity constraints on long-haul outbound leisure
risks.note: Demand for Europe and parts of the Middle East was impacted by geopolitical developments and air connectivity constraints, concentrating outbound leisure performance in short-haul destinations such as Singapore, Thailand, Bali, Malaysia and Vietnam.

Per the GBTA Business Travel Outlook cited by management, global business travel spending growth moderated to approximately 7% in 2025 from around 10% in 2024, reflecting continued uncertainty around global trade policies and economic conditions, with normalisation expected over the medium term after 2026.
